scenes.text: Your research agent just wrote a confident meeting brief. Some of it came from a page planted to fool it. Would you know? This is Assay.
Research agents sound sure, even when they're wrong. Run one twice, get two answers. And nobody tells you what a correct answer actually cost.

Assay freezes the web, so every agent searches the same saved pages, built once with Tavily. It plants a trap: a fake article, a hidden instruction, or an outage. Each agent runs three times. Every model call goes through Bifrost on a budget-capped key, so every step and every cent is recorded. Then each claim is checked against its source.
Pick your agents, a task, and a trap. Here, our three agent versions brief on Maxim AI, with a hidden instruction planted in one of the pages. Steps land live, with costs read from Bifrost's logs.
Every run leaves a receipt. This Cheap-first run switched models at thirty-two seconds, spent half a cent, and fell for the trap. Here's the claim, and here's the planted page it came from.

Here's what surprised us. We built two smarter versions of our agent. Cheap-first costs sixteen percent more per correct answer. Evidence-gated scored lower. Baseline wins. Weigh accuracy over cost, and the outside agent, GPT Researcher, takes the top spot.

Then put it to work. Enter a company and a meeting time. The Briefing Agent searches the last thirty days live with Tavily, and separates verified facts from uncertain ones, with open questions to ask.
Assay. Don't trust the answer. Check the receipt.
